newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says hoping for final decision on breakup soon.
newsitem.headline: NTT says hoping for final decision on breakup soon.

text.p: Japan's phone giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) said on Wednesday it hopes that a final decision will soon be made on the drawn-out wrangle over whether to break up the company.
NTT and the Posts Ministry will reveal in mid-December a rough outline of the company's future corporate structure, NTT president Junichiro Miyazu told a news conference.
Agreement on the future shape of NTT, the world's biggest telecoms company in terms of sales, would mark the end of a decade-long battle between its management and the government.
Splitting NTT into smaller companies and then setting up a holding company to unite them is one option, Miyazu said.
However, he declined to comment on how talks with the ministry were progressing.

Under this option, NTT's domestic long-distance and local phone operations would be broken up into three or four different businesses. Also, a new unit operating long-distance networks would be allowed to enter the international phone business.

Concerning the company's plan to enter the international phone business, Miyazu said the global market was changing so quickly that the company could not wait until Japan's NTT law had been revised to allow the company to start international operations.

The NTT law stipulates that the company, which is two-thirds owned by the government, must limit its operations to the domestic market. The firm dominates Japan's domestic phone networks, with a market share of 80 percent.
"The agreement (expected in the middle of December) might include a special clause regarding NTT's international business," Miyazu said.
The Posts Ministry has said it would not allow NTT to enter the international telecoms market unless it is split up into smaller companies.
A ministry panel proposed in February that NTT be broken up into three different companies.
